Probably yes, if closing costs are under about 3% (~$12k).

Assuming a 30-year loan at 5.9% versus 30 years at 6.5% (the payment is about $2,373 vs $2,528), you save about $155/month, or roughly $18.7k over 10 years. Breakeven is closing costs ÷ $155: $6k takes ~3 years, $10k ~5.4 years, $12k ~6.5 years. At typical costs of 2-3% ($8-12k), you net roughly $7-11k over your 10-year stay.

The strongest case against is the term reset. If you're several years into your current loan and refinance into a new 30-year, you restart the amortization clock and may pay more total interest over the full life, even with a lower payment. Fix this by choosing a term that matches your remaining years, or by paying the new loan at your old payment, which also pays it off faster. Also, if you might move or sell before about year 6, or if closing costs exceed ~$15k, it stops being worth it.

Don't count on rates dropping further, since that's unforecastable. If they do, you can refinance again, but only if you can recover another round of closing costs.

Get Loan Estimates from 2-3 lenders to compare the actual costs. If your current loan's remaining term or the quoted closing costs differ from my assumptions, send them and I'll rerun the numbers.
